column1: # How obtained: for each of the eight families named by 01-freeze-kind.md's
# table, grepped the family's existing Unit test file for (a) whether it
# already drives the family's occurrence-producing method through the
# family's OWN production code path (`->analyze()` for a Rule,
# `->toFindings()`/`->toFinding()` for a Finding-owned value object) rather
# than calling `OccurrenceKey::semantic()` directly, and (b) whether it
# already reads `->occurrenceKey?->value` off the resulting Finding. Counted
# every existing helper (fixture builder, in-memory metric bag, dependency/
# layer-match constructor) the file already carries, since a pin's cheapest
# form reuses an existing helper rather than adding a new one.
# What this method does not see: it does not prove a helper is *sufficient*
# for the specific pin assertion (e.g. an existing occurrenceKey mention may
# assert stability across two evidence values, not equality against a raw
# literal) — column 6 names the gap the new pin method still has to close.
# It also does not count wiring cost inside `AbstractCodeSmellRule`/
# `AbstractSecurityPatternRule` subclasses individually; family 7 and 8's
# price is estimated at the shared-factory level only (see their rows) and
# the per-rule question is left open, not decided, per 01-freeze-kind.md.
